text:
Registered residential sales reached 14,432 units valued at AED 42,635,071,625 in the last four weeks, a 41.5% increase over the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 5,985, recorded separately from sales. The median residential price per square foot stood at AED 1,689, up 1.4% from the previous four weeks. Off-plan transactions accounted for 57.7% of the volume, slightly below the 59.4% share seen in the preceding period.

Rental activity remained robust with 110,329 Ejari contracts registered. Renewals represented 51.6% of these contracts. The median annual residential rent was AED 68,729. In the top sales areas, Dubai South led with 3,364 sales over twelve weeks at a median of AED 1,685.8 per square foot. Jumeirah Village Circle followed with 2,495 sales at AED 1,424.9 per square foot. Down Town Jabal Ali recorded 1,458 sales at AED 1,740.5 per square foot.

Price momentum varied significantly across communities. Al Yufrah 1 showed the strongest heating with a 42.2% increase in median price per square foot over twelve weeks. Dubai Industrial City rose 10.0% and International City Phase 1 increased 8.2%. Conversely, Palm Jumeirah cooled by 16.7% and Jumeirah Lakes Towers declined 16.5%. Al Hebiah First dropped 13.2%. Highest estimated gross yields were found in Zaabeel First at 9.0% and International City Phase 1 at 8.6%.

Investors should monitor the 927 anomalous sales priced more than 35% away from comparable medians in the last 60 days. These figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts. Medians are used to mitigate the impact of outliers. Benchmark filters exclude bulk deals, partial-share transfers, portfolio blocks, mortgages, gifts, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
